class_evidence.ask_mechanism: The existing ask/how-many-entity rule and shared temporal question origo recognize a role-licensed timeperiod. A period-specific ask selects the matching timed event and rejects mixed timed/untimed evidence. An unscoped total sums across periods only when all scoped facts are explicitly timed non-state events with the same requested verb; state snapshots, cross-verb evidence, unresolved comparisons, and incomplete references decline.
class_evidence.premise_mechanism: The generic Quantity fold already emits event quantities. Its sentence-time extraction now accepts only a unique postverbal preposition/object pair that the existing adposition-role registry licenses as temporal-point for the governing verb and whose object is a timeperiod. It preserves the object's normalized fold as Quantity.time. Temporal-before, temporal-after, deadline, duration, start, end, ambiguous, multiple, and unlicensed attachments remain unstamped.
class_evidence.product_rationale: The user explicitly selected product-led manual mining after the curated Designer exposed a precision defect: 'Dara sold 4 books on Monday. Dara sold 6 books on Tuesday. How many books did Dara sell on Monday?' previously answered 10 because trailing calendar periods were discarded. The product requires useful, human-reviewable temporal event facts and conservative answers, independent of any GSM8K DEV yield.
structural_summary: The former curated behavior answered 10 for a Monday-only ask over Monday=4 and Tuesday=6 because both Quantity.time fields were null.
The boundary reuses temporal-point role licensing and the existing question reference-time seam; it adds no ask pattern and infers no temporal meaning from arbitrary prepositions.
The positive total class is same-holder, same-measure, same-verb, explicitly timed, non-state event quantities across distinct periods.
State snapshots remain non-additive across periods; a period-specific state ask selects its exact snapshot, while an unscoped total declines.
Calendar weekdays and eleven unambiguous month names moved from difg-mined to core-english without changing combined-registry semantics; modal/month 'may' remains excluded.

implementation_contract.class_justification: This is one complete semantic boundary: exact-period preservation and selection for postverbal calendar-point event quantities, plus the narrowly related unscoped total over those same independently asserted events. Moving the already-supported calendar family to core-english is required for the curated Designer to read and generate the class and is coupled to the fact/ask support so vocabulary is never admitted without a usable semantic path.

mechanism: Preserve one unambiguous postverbal temporal-point PP on Quantity facts, use the existing shared temporal question origo for period-specific asks, and permit an unscoped cross-period sum only when every scoped quantity is an explicitly timed non-state event with the requested verb.
risks: A broad postverbal time heuristic could stamp location, deadline, duration, before/after, or ambiguous attachments as exact event time; only the existing temporal-point role licenses it.
A broad total relaxation could add state snapshots, different verbs, untimed evidence, or partial comparative facts; all continue to decline.

Moving calendar vocabulary could change the combined core-english plus difg-mined registry or reintroduce capitalization/name ambiguity; the synthetic gate proves semantic equivalence and singular ownership.
The ambiguous surface 'may' remains a modal in core and absent from timeperiod.
More than one distinct temporal-point attachment is not collapsed into an arbitrary period.

Necessary adjacent scope drift: src/rulekit/kernel/guards.py makes answer accounting inspect the same temporal-origo scope as the consumer; without it a correct Tuesday answer is vetoed by intentionally filtered Monday evidence.

Necessary mechanical test drift: twelve historical generator/frontier assertions move only from 267 to 285 reachable fillers, exactly accounting for the eighteen core calendar identities; rule coverage, ordering, and generated behavior are otherwise unchanged.
